chapter: Fellow musicians: Kirk, Bunk, Parker, McShann
title: Why Bunk Johnson passed through Kansas City
summary: Smith and Lovett say Bunk played at the Yellow Front but did not come to stay or look for work.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: You know, about this time that we're talking about -- well, to get back to Thamon Hayes, Major and Basie, Bunk Johnson was in town. Now-- when I was in Washington, Baby, they said that you had played with him but I think they thought you'd played with him in New Orleans when indeed you never did, you played with him here in Kansas City.
-- which must have had terrific music
because so many great men played there.
What was Bunk Johnson doing in Kansas City and why didn't one of these bands pick him up like Thomas or Benny?
Well, I don't think he came in to stay, you know, he didn't come to stay. It's hard to get those guys out of New Orleans, man, I'll tell you that.
I don't think he was looking for work.
No, he wasn't looking for work. They had a hard time getting me from Louisiana, you know. Man I wanted to go back. I come near crying to go back home.
